newsitem.title: NORWAY: Denmark to adopt new oil licensing policy-Statoil.
newsitem.headline: Denmark to adopt new oil licensing policy-Statoil.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday that Denmark would adopt a new "open door" policy for oil and gas exploration licences from May.

Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said oil companies would be able to seek exploration licences at any time of the year after May 20 in all of Denmark's mainland and inshore waters as well as the Danish sector of the North Sea.
The new regulations did not cover the Central Graben area to the west on the Danish continental shelf.
"Applications can be submitted to the Danish Energy Agency between January 2 and September 30 every year. Licences will be awarded at any time," Statoil said.
It said the new policy was partly intended to encourage smaller companies with new ideas to apply for licences without risking competition with other applicants in a licensing round.
Denmark has so far held four offshore licensing rounds, with a fifth due to open later this year with a deadline for applications next January.
